page_title: A little space. For what matters.

summary.name: Posato
summary.one_liner: Posato is a focus app that blocks chosen websites and apps for a timed pause or scheduled pauses on Mac, iPhone, Linux, and Android, with no account and no Posato-operated server.
use_cases: Pause distracting websites and apps during work blocks
Schedule recurring focus time such as weekday mornings
Block distracting sites on a Linux desktop
Limit app use on an Android phone during a pause
Sync focus sets across Mac and iPhone with iCloud
Share pause sets across devices through a folder such as Dropbox
summary.what_it_does: Posato lets you group websites (exact domains) and, per device, apps into pause sets. You start a timed pause from 5 minutes to 24 hours, pick a preset such as 25 minutes or until end of day, or set a recurring schedule that runs on each device you set up. Overlapping pauses combine, and each item stays blocked until the last pause including it ends. Sync is available via iCloud between one Mac and one iPhone, or via an encrypted folder shared through services like Dropbox or Syncthing. Pause sets can also be exported to a .posato file, optionally protected with a code.
notable: Encrypted sync via iCloud or any shared folder, with no Posato account or server
Schedules run on each device without the app window open
Pause sets keep websites shared while app choices stay on each device
Source is on GitHub, with releases downloadable from GitHub Releases
caveats: Posato adds deliberate friction and is not an unbreakable lock
Website blocking can be bypassed by browser DNS over HTTPS, strict Private DNS on Android, or Private Relay-type features
iPhone restrictions can linger after a session ends; sessions under 15 minutes clear only when Posato is open at the end or next opened
Paused apps are quit on Mac and Linux, so unsaved work must be saved first
